subject: Quick follow-up: discovery recap and pilot next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir.khanna@brightlane.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + suggested pilot next steps

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed next step so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what you described:
- Pain: high latency and unpredictable inference cost on your customer search model at 1–5k QPS.
- Constraints: legal requires audit logs and VPC isolation for PII; budget window opens mid-November.
- Success criteria: P50 latency under 120ms and token cost < $0.001 for ranker path; integration with existing vector store (Pinecone).

What Redwood proposed:
- Two-week pilot using a tuned open model on Dedicated (reserved) capacity to validate latency and cost at a small-scale production load.
- Technical sync between our infra engineer and your ML infra owner to validate KV/cache integration and trace headers.
- Deliverables: pilot runbook, performance report, and a ballpark SOW for scaling to production.

Immediate next steps I recommend:
1) Share one week of anonymized request traces and a 1000-row sample of vectors (we’ll accept a sanitized CSV).
2) 30-min technical sync with your ML infra engineer — proposed window: Oct 5–8.
3) I’ll follow up with a short pilot estimate and runbook (attached).

Attachments: redwood-discovery-recap.pdf (short summary), pilot-estimate.xlsx (initial numbers).

If this looks right, can you confirm who on your side should join the technical sync and whether the Oct 5–8 window works? If priority has shifted, a quick note helps us avoid unnecessary follow-up.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov | Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

P.S. Ben (cc) will be on the technical sync and can pull the pilot runbook together once we confirm the data sample.
